text:
Connor Hellebuyck's first shutout as a Devil came in Toronto, 23 saves in a 4-0 win, and it arrived on the same night New Jersey told him he wouldn't start in Winnipeg on Tuesday. GM Sunny Mehta said Hellebuyck was adamant he felt a duty to play there, and that the team decided otherwise. The Devils have now won five straight, and the goalie they traded for on Oct. 23 is a big part of why.

The game itself was closer than the score. Toronto had more of the five-on-five play, 54 shot attempts to 45 and 1.81 expected goals to 1.49, and the Devils deserved to win 59% of the time. The difference was finish and the net: Hellebuyck saved about two goals more than his shots deserved, and Anthony Stolarz gave up three on 28.

Timo Meier did the scoring early. He snapped one in at 8:28 of the second and tipped in a Jack Hughes setup at 12:44, and New Jersey's win chance went from 48% to 85% in four minutes. Nico Hischier's power-play goal in the third, on a 56% look from Hughes and Jesper Bratt, was his 500th career point, a nice number for the first pick of the 2017 draft. Connor Brown added the last one late. Toronto never had a power play.

For the Maple Leafs this was the back half of a bad weekend: a loss to Montreal on Saturday, then nothing to show here, with Kirill Marchenko among the regulars out. New Jersey played the night before too, beating the Islanders in overtime on Long Island, and looked like the fresher team anyway. That's what a five-game run does.
headline: Hellebuyck shuts out Toronto, then gets Winnipeg off
